long_biography.plain_text:
Raised in modest circumstances in Tatamagouche, Nova Scotia, Joyce left school at sixteen and moved to Hamilton with little money. Factory work, naval service and a period as a police constable preceded his move into food service. He took over the first Tim Hortons restaurant, became Tim Horton's partner and, after Horton's death, gained control of the chain. Under Joyce, franchising turned the single-store opportunity into a national institution.

The sale to Wendy's shifted Joyce from restaurant operator to diversified investor and philanthropist. Through Jetport and Fox Harb'r, he developed aviation, real-estate and resort interests. He also helped establish the Tim Horton Children's Foundation and later the Joyce Family Foundation, directing substantial support toward camps, hospitals and education. Appointed to the Order of Canada, he died in 2019 at age eighty-eight.
